# Safety Checks

The repository runs runtime sanitizers and CodeQL on pushes and pull requests
targeting `master`.

| Workflow | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| [`sanitizers.yml`](sanitizers.yml) | Linux ASan (C++11 and C++20), TSan (C++20), and UBSan (C++17); Windows/MSVC ASan (C++20). Each job builds and runs CTest. |
| [`codeql.yml`](codeql.yml) | C++ security and quality queries on pushes, pull requests, and a weekly schedule. Results appear in GitHub's code scanning view. |

The sanitizer jobs upload test logs when they fail. TSan can expose races in
the reader's worker and queue paths; ASan and UBSan cover memory and undefined
behavior errors. These are separate jobs because their instrumentation has
different runtime requirements.

## Local sanitizer run

On Linux, configure a separate build directory for each sanitizer. For example:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/asan -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DCSV_CXX_STANDARD=20 \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g" \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g"
cmake --build build/asan
ctest --test-dir build/asan --output-on-failure
```

Substitute `-fsanitize=thread` or `-fsanitize=undefined` in both flag values
to reproduce the corresponding Linux job. For Windows/MSVC ASan, use the
configuration in [`sanitizers.yml`](sanitizers.yml); it also sets linker flags
needed by that job.

## Optimized single-header distribution

The generator owns the entire generation pipeline. With the Clang-enabled
`single_header` 1.2.0 package, run:

```sh
single_header --config single_header.json
```

The config selects all optimizations, compiler arguments, and the alternate
platform declaration. Output is `build/distribution/csv.hpp`; the generator
writes its stitching report alongside it. Relative compiler arguments resolve
from the config directory. No Python interpreter, CMake analysis build,
compilation-database wrapper, or CSV-specific validation script is needed.

The [shared generation action](../actions/optimized-single-header/action.yml)
uses the released Linux Clang-backend package, which includes the driver,
compiler resource headers, and LLVM/Clang runtime libraries. Generation runners
need their usual platform C++ standard-library and system headers. They do not
build the generator or install an LLVM development SDK. Other-platform
lightweight packages remain available for ordinary amalgamation.

The generator performs its own compiler validation while inserting `inline`
and stitching definitions. Include deduplication, namespace merging and cleanup
are configured in `single_header.json`. Its explicit mixed-include list covers
standard headers already required unconditionally; `<thread>` remains guarded.

Compiler matrices download the header generated by their own workflow run.
CMake's `generate_single_header` target copies that artifact, or directly invokes
`single_header` with the config when an executable is supplied. Existing compiler,
exception-mode and compatibility jobs test the generated header. Generation and
release publication do not repeat that consumer test matrix or require particular
functions to stitch, include counts, or namespace counts.

Release publication checks out the requested tag, generates once, writes a
SHA-256 checksum, and uploads the header, checksum and stitching report.
Documentation uses the same action. The Python package and publishing workflow
are maintained separately.
